document.title: UBL Update
document.publisher: National Security Archive (GWU), The Central Intelligence Agency 9/11 File: Hundreds of Secret Agency Documents on Osama Bin Laden Declassified
document.note: CIA update on bin Laden. Includes the warning that a UBL attack against U.S. interests could occur at any time or place and that CIA is unlikely to have prior warning. Cited in 9/11 Commission Report Chapter 4, Endnote 188.

persons.name: Usama bin Ladin
persons.role: Leader of the organization that is the subject of the briefing; target of disruption and capture planning
persons.status_detail: Alive at the time of the document (Aug 1999)

organizations.notes: The slides state that once UBL gives approval, his organization could launch an attack with no additional warning. The group is not named as al-Qa'ida in the legible text.

organizations.name: Central Intelligence Agency
organizations.notes: Author of the briefing. It plans operations to disrupt UBL and to capture him.

events.description: Africa Bombings. The slides mention the 7 August anniversary as a possible attack date. The year is inferred.
US retaliatory missile strike. The slides mention the 20 August anniversary as a possible attack date. The year is inferred.
The threat-assessment slide lists 7 August and the Africa Bombings. The year is inferred from the 1998 East Africa embassy bombings, and the slide appears to treat 7 August as an anniversary date.
The slide lists 20 August next to a 'retaliatory missile' strike on UBL. The year is inferred from the August 1998 US retaliation.

relationships.detail: The organization could launch attacks once UBL gives approval.

key_claims: A UBL attack against US interests could occur at any time.
The US is unlikely to have prior warning of the timing or place of a UBL attack.
Once UBL gives approval, his organization could launch an attack with no additional warning.
The anniversaries of the 7 August Africa bombings and the 20 August retaliatory missile strike are flagged as possible attack dates.
Reporting on UBL is good, but a capture is unlikely because of the risks involved.
A new group needs to be identified to undertake a capture operation.
